AI content on Australian tour website sends tourists chasing hot springs that don’t exist
item.description: An Australian tour company’s AI-generated article falsely promoted “Weldborough Hot Springs” in Tasmania, sending confused tourists to a town with no such attraction. Owner Scott Hennessy admitted the error, citing outsourced AI content and insufficient in-house resources. The incident highlights the growing risks of AI travel advice, where invented destinations and inaccuracies are increasingly misleading travellers worldwide.

IS owns up 'suicide attack' on Pakistan Shia mosque; toll now 36
item.description: The Islamic State has claimed responsibility for a deadly blast at a Shia mosque in Islamabad, which resulted in over three dozen casualties. The terror outfit's mouthpiece stated the attack was a Fidayeen operation by a soldier of the Islamic State in Pakistan Province. This claim comes amidst growing sectarian tensions and an IS call for Lashkar-e-Taiba members to defect.

Did Tony Hawk’s wedding take place on Jeffrey Epstein’s island? Skateboarding legend responds
item.description: Skateboarding legend Tony Hawk has publicly debunked claims linking him to Jeffrey Epstein’s private island. The confusion arose from a third-party FBI tip and a photographer named Mark Epstein who captured Hawk’s 2006 Fiji wedding. Hawk clarified the timeline of his four marriages, confirmed he never visited Epstein’s property, and called the online speculation “nonsense,” stressing the importance of verifiable facts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Mixed emotions’: Team USA skier Hunter Hess says wearing the flag doesn’t mean backing all US policies, sparks Olympic boycott calls
item.description: American freestyle skiers Hunter Hess and Chris Lillis expressed mixed feelings about representing the US at the Winter Olympics, citing domestic issues they disagree with. Their comments sparked backlash online, with some viewers vowing to boycott the Games, arguing that wearing the flag signifies full endorsement of the country.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Twitch star Emiru shares thoughts on female streamers copying her style
item.description: Popular Twitch streamer Emiru sparked discussion with her recent comments about other streamers who share her distinctive look and fashion. She humorously questioned collaborations with those who resemble her, touching on themes of originality and credit within the online content creation space. Her remarks have ignited conversations among fans about imitation versus inspiration among female streamers.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Twitch streamer Bisscute hospitalized after katana accident on live stream
item.description: Popular streamer Bisscute suffered a severe hand injury during a live broadcast when a katana slipped from its sheath. Instinctively trying to catch the falling blade, she cut two tendons in her middle and ring fingers, requiring surgery. Despite the painful accident, Bisscute has shown remarkable resilience, already sporting a cast and reassuring fans of her well-being.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: UK rapper Central Cee confirms conversion to Islam and reveals new name during livestream
item.description: British rapper Central Cee has confirmed he has converted to Islam and changed his name, revealing the decision during a low-key livestream. The artist, formerly Oakley Caesar-Su, said he had taken the Shahada and adopted the name Akhil. Fans and members of the Muslim community welcomed the announcement, which followed years of subtle references in his music and online posts.

item.title: Ofcom revokes TV licences of Overseas Friends of BJP (UK) president
item.description: UK's Ofcom has revoked broadcasting licences for MATV National and MATV Music, held by Middlesex Broadcasting Corporation Limited. The regulator determined that MATV Broadcasting Ltd, where Kuldeep Shekhawat is a director, exercised editorial control, not the licence holder. Ofcom cited Shekhawat's role as president of Overseas Friends of BJP (UK) as a potential disqualification due to political affiliations.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Canton

item.title: UK considers targeting Russia’s ‘shadow fleet’ in new escalation against Moscow
item.description: Britain is exploring military options to seize Russia-linked shadow fleet tankers, potentially opening a new front against Moscow as its oil revenues decline. This comes after the US seized a similar vessel. While international law allows for challenging stateless ships, escalatory risks have so far prevented action, despite Royal Marines expressing readiness.
